terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation (short a: dare, datum)
terms.comment: The thing in the accusative and the person in the dative: dā mihi pilam. The a is short in every form except dās and dā.

evidence: Catull. 1.1: cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum?
terms.comment: alicui aliquid dōnāre, or aliquem aliquā rē dōnāre, to present someone with something.
Of passing something from one person’s hands to another’s.

phrases.latin: ut puerīs ōlim dant crūstula blandī doctōrēs, elementa velint ut discere prīma
phrases.english: as coaxing teachers sometimes give children biscuits, so that they will want to learn their letters

phrases.latin: cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum āridā modo pūmice expolītum?
phrases.english: Whom shall I give this charming new little book to, just polished with dry pumice?

sources: Lewis & Short: do · Lewis & Short: dono · Lewis & Short: trado
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-catullus, loci-horatius, loci-martialis, loci-gellius), checked against the editions named there.
